schema.description: Structured result produced by the Decision Gate Topology Agent. It returns the updated normal-flow topology with inserted decision gates and a revision request for unresolved questions.

decision_gate_topology_draft.description: Updated normal-flow topology. The nodes array contains the inherited MAIN_FLOW_POINT nodes and the inserted DECISION_GATE nodes.

topology_status.description: Current review status of the decision-gate topology.

decision_gates.description: Complete mixed topology node list. Connections may reference a wfpoint_id, decision_gate_id, or outcome_id.

revision_request.description: Review fields returned for the user to complete. The agent creates confirmation questions but leaves all user-editable answer fields empty.

confirmation_questions.description: Concrete questions whose answers may confirm, correct, or complete the decision-gate topology.

additional_user_context.description: User-editable additional context. The agent must return an empty string.

main_flow_point_node.description: A high-level normal-flow point inherited from the input topology. Existing identifiers and semantics should be preserved unless the topology is explicitly revised.

wfpoint_id.description: Stable identifier of the normal-flow point, such as mfp_001.

node_type.description: Node discriminator for a normal-flow point.

name.description: Short human-readable name of the normal-flow point.

description.description: Explanation of what this normal-flow point represents in the workflow topology.

previous_node_ids.description: References that flow into this node. Values may reference wfpoint_id, decision_gate_id, or outcome_id. When this node follows a decision gate, the relevant outcome_id should normally be used.

next_node_ids.description: References that follow this node. Values may reference wfpoint_id or decision_gate_id. When a decision gate is inserted after this node, the decision_gate_id should be used.

confidence.description: Confidence that this node correctly represents its place in the normal-flow topology.

decision_gate_node.description: A high-level control point inserted into the normal-flow topology where the workflow selects, blocks, redirects, delays, confirms, or finalizes a path.

decision_gate_id.description: Stable identifier of the decision gate, such as dg_001.

node_type.description: Node discriminator for a decision gate.

name.description: Short human-readable name of the decision gate, suitable for graph visualization.

decision_question.description: Concrete question answered by this gate. This field expresses the central meaning of the decision.

decision_responsibility.description: Explanation of what this gate is responsible for determining in the workflow.

anchored_to_node_ids.description: MAIN_FLOW_POINT identifiers that flow directly into this decision gate and to which the gate is semantically attached. These values map to canonical previousNodeIds.

decision_basis.description: Dynamically generated, workflow-specific factors, conditions, evidence, confirmations, checks, or criteria used to answer the decision question.

decision_nature_tags.description: Controlled semantic categories describing the nature of the decision. Every item must be selected from the configured vocabulary; new tags must not be invented.

outcomes.description: Logical possible results of this decision gate. Each outcome acts as an output port and may connect to existing nodes, request a missing branch, remain unresolved, or leave the current workflow scope.

confidence.description: Confidence that this decision gate correctly represents a meaningful macro-level control point.

decision_gate_outcome.description: A logical result of a DECISION_GATE. The outcome may already be attached, may require a new branch, may remain unresolved, or may terminate or leave the parent workflow scope.

outcome_id.description: Stable identifier formed from the parent gate identifier and a sequential suffix, such as dg_001_out_001.

outcome_label.description: Short machine-readable label for the outcome, written in snake_case.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the conditions and meaning of this outcome.

connection_status.description: Configured state of the connection between this outcome and the remaining topology.

branch_creation_request.description: Request describing a missing continuation branch. Must contain an object when connection_status is branch_candidate_needed and must otherwise be null.

next_node_ids.description: Existing topology nodes reached through this outcome. For attached outcomes this must contain an existing node reference. For branch_candidate_needed, unresolved, or terminal_or_out_of_scope it may be empty.

branch_creation_request.description: Structured request for the normal-flow topology agent or another topology revision agent to create a missing branch for an outcome.

requested_branch_purpose.description: What the missing branch should represent and why it is needed.

expected_start_context.description: Where and under what decision outcome or operational condition the branch should begin.

expected_end_or_merge_behavior.description: How the branch may end, merge back, enter waiting, redirect, leave scope, or preserve unresolved alternatives.

confirmation_question.description: A concrete user question required to resolve a material ambiguity in the decision-gate topology.

question_id.description: Stable sequential identifier for the question, such as cq_001.

question.description: The concrete question to present to the user.

why_needed.description: Explanation of why the answer matters for the correctness of the topology.

related_node_ids.description: Identifiers of the MAIN_FLOW_POINT, DECISION_GATE, or outcome elements affected by this question.

blocks_next_pass.description: Whether this unresolved question prevents downstream processing from continuing safely.

answer.description: User-editable answer. The agent must return an empty string.
